headline: Stormy week of wind, rain, and coastal flooding; a weekend break is uncertain.
summary: A slow-moving low-pressure system offshore is steering a series of Pacific storm fronts into western Washington, and the pattern stays active. Southeast winds ahead of each front bring repeated rounds of rain to the lowlands and snow to the higher passes. The strongest wind and surf are on the coast and islands, and coastal flooding from high tides and surf peaks Tuesday, with concern continuing through Thursday. Another widespread rain system arrives Wednesday night into Thursday, and rivers will rise, with the Skokomish likely reaching flood stage midweek. Temperatures run above average, with highs in the 50s. Later, a ridge of high pressure aloft may bring a brief weekend break, but its strength and position are uncertain.
changes: Coastal flooding now peaks Tuesday rather than Wednesday, and coastal flood watches cover Seattle and the Puget Sound lowlands from Tuesday night through Thursday. The possible break has moved from Friday to the weekend, and forecasters remain unsure about it.
